You must understand both the historical narrative and the pedagogical innovations.</Callout>

blocks.raw: <Tip>Bauhaus = founded 1919 by Gropius in Weimar; three distinct directors (Gropius 1919–1928, Meyer 1928–1930, Mies 1930–1933); unified art, craft, industry through pedagogy. Key principle: teach thinking and principles, not style or copying. Remember: 1919 founding, 1925 move to Dessau, 1933 Nazi closure.</Tip>

blocks.raw: <Note>The Bauhaus was NOT a style school—it never developed a recognizable "Bauhaus style." It was a pedagogy and philosophy that taught principles applicable across any medium. This is essential: students learned principles of composition, color, proportion, and human behavior that could be applied to architecture, furniture, typography, textiles, ceramics, or graphic design. The diversity of Bauhaus output reflects this principle-based, not style-based, approach.</Note>

blocks.raw: <Warn>Critical: Don't confuse the three Bauhaus periods. Gropius (1919–1928) was experimental and artistic. Meyer (1928–1930) was functionalist and socially radical. Mies (1930–1933) was austere, geometric, and formally rigorous. Each director brought a distinct philosophy—the Bauhaus evolved through its directorate. There is no single "Bauhaus identity"; it changed with leadership.</Warn>

blocks.raw: <ExamTip>**Pattern 2: Director and Philosophy.** You may see: "Which Bauhaus director emphasized social responsibility and functionalism, arguing that design should serve working-class needs?" Answer: Hannes Meyer. Or: "Which director brought geometric austerity and focused on fundamental design principles?" Answer: Mies van der Rohe. You must associate each director with their distinct approach.</ExamTip>

blocks.raw: <ExamTip>**Pattern 3: Building and Institution.** You may see: "The Bauhaus Building in Dessau (1925–1926) is significant because [A] it housed the largest design school in Europe [B] it demonstrated Bauhaus principles through its own design [C] it rejected modernism in favor of tradition [D] it was designed by Mies van der Rohe." Answer: B. The building is both shelter and teaching tool.</ExamTip>
